abstract: Questionnaires on sexual function, marital status, and fertility were returned by 84 men who received radiotherapy for seminoma (Stage I, II, or III). The mean length of follow-up was ten years. Although 93 per cent were married, 19 per cent had low rates of sexual activity, 12 per cent reported low sexual desire, 15 per cent had erectile dysfunction, 10 per cent had difficulty reaching orgasm, and 14 per cent had premature ejaculation. The most common problems were reduced intensity of orgasm (33%) and reduced semen volume (49%). Twenty-one men remained childless, and 30 per cent of men worried at least occasionally about infertility. Thirteen children were conceived after cancer therapy. The data suggest that sexual dysfunction and infertility are important concerns for a subgroup of men treated for seminoma.
abstract_ja: セミノーマ（病期I、II、III）に対して放射線療法を受けた男性84名から、性機能、婚姻状況、妊孕性に関するアンケートの回答を得た。平均追跡期間は10年であった。93%が既婚であったが、性行為の頻度が低い者が19%、性欲低下が12%、勃起障害が15%、オルガズム到達困難が10%、早漏が14%であった。最も多い問題は、オルガズムの強度低下（33%）と精液量の減少（49%）であった。21名が子どもを持たず、30%の男性は少なくとも時々不妊について心配していた。治療後に13名の子どもが生まれた。これらのデータは、セミノーマの治療を受けた男性の一部にとって、性機能障害と不妊が重要な懸念であることを示唆する。
